articles.title: LeBron James' son Bryce gets first taste of Arizona basketball as Wildcats begin showing their hand
articles.summary: Bryce James started Arizona’s first three games, then watched the next two from the bench.
articles.body: Bryce James started Arizona’s first three games, then watched the next two from the bench. The redshirt freshman and youngest son of LeBron James did not play at Auburn last Friday or in the 85-79 win over No. 3 UConn on Wednesday. Coach Tommy Lloyd has said the 6-foot-5 guard is healthy and that game flow kept him out. Before that, James averaged 2.7 points in 12.3 minutes. Arizona is 4-1 now, and Lloyd says the staff will keep looking for ways to get him back on the floor.Why is Bryce James getting fewer minutes at Arizona?The short answer is the rotation. Arizona beat UConn 85-79 for the Huskies’ first loss, and Lloyd rode his starters to do it. All five reached double figures behind 20 points from Ivan Kharchenkov. Only three reserves played, for 17 minutes combined. James was not one of them, just as he was not at Auburn last Friday.Lloyd spoke about that one afterward. “I wish I would have got him in the game,” he said. Arizona had built a lead playing one way, Auburn rallied, and Lloyd felt it was hard to throw in a player who had barely been on the court. He went with the group that had earned the lead.Nothing points to an injury, and the opponent explains plenty. UConn came in ranked third, so the starters stayed on the floor. The change stands out. The guard was in the opening five for the first three games, and Lloyd had been sorting his rotation while forward RJ Godfrey waited on word about his eligibility.What James has shown when he has playedThe flashes are real, even if the minutes are small. Against Northern Arizona on Nov. 10, James swung over to block a two-handed dunk attempt from Lucas Toukam, and the McKale Center crowd roared. He knocked down a 3-pointer from the wing shortly after. Arizona won that game 90-59.The passing has stood out too. He threw a no-look pass to Ugnius Jarusevicius for a layup in that game and a fast-break bounce pass to Kharchenkov against UCLA. Lloyd has also said the guard has shown him a lot over the past couple of weeks.His father has noticed. LeBron posted on Instagram after a game, writing “1% each day Young” with a crown emoji. The son came in as a three-star recruit from Sierra Canyon and spent last season as a redshirt while Arizona reached the Final Four. The defense is where he helps most right now, and the offense is still catching up. Lloyd has kept the spotlight off him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball Rookie Report: Tiered rankings for top 1st-year players one month into the 2026-27 NBA season
articles.summary: Dan Titus groups the top rookies into tiers based on fantasy basketball production in both points leagues and 9-cat formats.
articles.body:
Rookies are usually a patience game, but this class is producing in November. To compare their value across formats, I averaged each rookie's Yahoo Fantasy 9-cat and standard points ranks into a composite. Both rankings are league-wide, not rookie-only, so a rank of 66 means 66th in fantasy value — not 66th among rookies.

The two formats reward different strengths: efficiency and balanced contributions matter more in 9-cat, while volume drives points-league value. The composite offers a snapshot across both, while the gap between ranks shows which format suits each player best. I also included true shooting percentage, which accounts for 3s and free throws to give a fuller picture of scoring efficiency than field goal percentage alone.

Here's the first rookie report of the 2026-27 season.

Cameron Boozer - PF/C - Memphis Grizzlies

Boozer is the best rookie in the class by composite (40.5) and in 9-cat (47th), and his 34th ranking in points is only behind Darius Acuff Jr. among rookies. He's at 9.4 boards and 5.3 assists with 16.6 points in 31.1 minutes, and that kind of big-man passing is rare, especially for a first-year player. The 40% shooting is the one number holding him back, but 88.9% from the line and 1.9 3s a game lift his true shooting to 53.5%. His 14.1% rebound rate is the highest of any rookie on this list.

I touted Bulls F Caleb Wilson as the player with the highest ceiling, but Boozer looks like he could be right there as a consistent double-double threat with the added bonus of high-end playmaking for fantasy managers. A cool record that he's pacing toward: he'd be the first rookie forward to average 15-10-5, and only the second rookie to do it since the "Big O" Oscar Robertson in 1960-61.

Yaxel Lendeborg - SF/PF - Golden State Warriors

Lendeborg is right behind Boozer, ranking 42nd in points and 87th in 9-cat for a 64.5 composite as one of the most complete rookies in the class. He's at 20.8 points on 46.4% shooting with 7.3 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.1 steals, and his 26.4% usage rate shows Golden State is running things through him. His 58.1% true shooting is the best of the five rookies who use at least 24% of their team's possessions. He gets to the line nearly six times a game, so there's a floor even when the shot isn't falling. With Stephen Curry out, expect Yaxel to build on his early-season success as the primary engine of Golden State's offense.

Tier 2: Scorers still finding their shot

Everyone in this tier is shooting under 42%, but their true shooting sits around 53%, so the damage is smaller than it looks. The question is what each one gives you while the shot comes around. For Acuff, it's points, assists and 3s: 26.0 points, 7.0 assists and 3.3 3s in 36.7 minutes, with a 32.5% usage rate that is like a veteran's workload. Despite his ball-hog persona, he's assisted on 34.2% of his teammates' baskets while on the floor — the highest rate of any rookie and 15th in the NBA. The price is 41% shooting on 22.6 attempts (52.9% true shooting) with 3.9 turnovers and limited stocks. Even with that, he's 88th in 9-cat, which is a strong result for a rookie shooting this poorly and shows how much his counting stats carry him. In points leagues, he's 24th, so he's a top-30 player there and a clear starter across formats.

Wilson is out 4-6 weeks with a right metacarpal fracture, but his 10 games before the injury were strong: 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.8 steals, 0.9 blocks and 2.3 3s in 30.8 minutes. That scoring-stocks-and-boards profile is the hardest to find amongst this specific rookie class. If Norman Powell gets traded (his contract is movable), Wilson would become Chicago's primary scorer. Combine that with his versatility and he'd be a player well worth trading for and stashing on IL.

Peterson's route to fantasy prominence is through scoring, assists and 3s. It's happening sooner than expected, as his opportunity share is expanding with injuries to Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. It's left him as Utah's second scoring option, with a chance to be the primary one until they return. He's at 16.5 points, 2.2 3s, and 1.1 steals in 30.6 minutes and he shoots 84.0% from the line. He also protects the ball better than the other high-usage rookies in the top two tiers, with a turnover rate of 10.4 per 100 possessions, compared to 13.0 to 16.9 for the rest. Peterson's sporting a 29.2% usage rate with Markkanen off the floor (19.9% with him), so a natural jump in production will push Peterson into a top-100 asset in 9-cat and top-75 in points pretty quickly.

Meleek Thomas - SG - Cleveland Cavaliers

Thomas is the most efficient scorer in this tier, with 13.4 points, 2.6 3s and 1.2 steals in 23.9 minutes on 47.5% shooting. The second-rounder has been one of the Cavs' best weapons off the bench, connecting on 44% of his 3s, while 54% of his shots come from beyond the arc. He's seeing a healthy 21% usage rate but only turns it over 1.2 times a game. There aren't many ways for him to hurt you, which explains why he's the highest-ranked rookie in this tier in 9-cat. He's a good add in 12-team leagues.

Aday Mara is picking up steam, averaging 12.5 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.5 blocks in 26.5 minutes over his last six games while shooting 68% from the field. He's scored in double figures in all six contests, raising his season averages to 9.2 points, 6.5 boards and 1.7 blocks. The recent production makes him worth a look for fantasy managers seeking rebounds, blocks and a field-goal percentage boost, though his 57.7% shooting from the line remains a drawback. At 50% rostered, shallow league managers should consider him, especially given Isaiah Hartenstein's injury history.

Dybantsa is the most interesting gap in the class: 216th in 9-cat and 85th in points. He's playing heavy minutes (33.8 per night), and at 16.3 points, 6.6 rebounds, 2.3 dimes and 1.3 steals per game, the volume is there. What's missing is efficiency, at 41.6% from the field and 71.9% from the line, which hurts a 9-cat build far more than it does in points leagues. That's more of a shooting problem than a role problem, so I'd buy him now in points leagues and be more patient in 9-cat.

Keaton Wagler - SG, Los Angeles Clippers

Wagler's main fantasy value comes at the free-throw line and 3s, where he shoots 85.9% on 5.5 attempts per game while averaging 12.5 points overall. The 37.0% shooting is an issue, and he's not providing much beyond scoring (6 combined rebounds and assists per game). However, it's a long season and the Clippers will likely increase his minutes and usage as the season progresses.

These four are 12-team options to keep on your watchlist or get a jump on before your leaguemates do.

Where the rookie class stands one month in

Lendeborg and Boozer claim the top spots one month into the season, with Acuff's counting stats pushing him into the top tier. He is, after all, the best points-league rookie by a wide margin. Peterson and Mara's growing roles give them upside, and Dybantsa is one of my trade targets for points leagues. Be on the lookout for Flemings now that CJ McCollum will miss four weeks, and the more the Bucks lose, the more Burries' minutes will increase as the season goes on.

I'll update this report monthly as roles and production settle. Until then, prioritize steady minutes and production over draft pedigree.

articles.title: ‘You gonna let them win?’: Stephen A. Smith sparks race row over Lakers’ championship chances
articles.summary: Stephen A.
articles.body: Stephen A. Smith is facing fresh criticism after questioning whether Black NBA players will allow the Los Angeles Lakers to win a championship because three of the team’s leading players are white. Smith made the remarks on ESPN’s First Take on Wednesday, November 18, as the Lakers held a 13-2 record. ESPN analyst Jay Williams called the comments disturbing and said they brought back the kind of thinking sports had spent generations trying to leave behind. Smith later pushed back at Williams on X and said he stood by his words and his original view.Jay Williams Calls Stephen A. Smith’s Lakers Comments DisturbingSmith’s latest remarks followed comments on his podcast the previous week. He said he had never seen an NBA champion led by three white players and predicted the Lakers would not win the title this season.The team’s leading trio is Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler. Smith has praised their ability, but keeps bringing up their race when explaining his doubts about their title chances.On Wednesday’s First Take, Smith praised the Lakers’ strong start and named head coach JJ Redick as a possible Coach of the Year. He then turned to Black players around the league.“I’m looking at the brothers, and I’m saying, LA doing special things… these white brothers can play, y’all gonna let them win a championship?” Smith asked.Williams, an ESPN basketball analyst who sometimes appears on First Take, criticised the remarks in a post on X. He compared Smith’s words to racial talk from the 1930s and 1940s.Williams said athletes had spent generations fighting to be judged by talent rather than skin color. He questioned why Black players were being asked whether they should allow white players to win.“At what point does fighting against discrimination turn into perpetuating the same mentality we fought so hard to overcome?” Williams wrote.Stephen A. Smith Stands by His Words as Fans Push BackSmith responded on X and made it clear that Williams had not changed his mind. He thanked his colleague but said the comparison with the 1930s did not address his point.“I love this challenge to the fellas,” Smith wrote. “I want to see if this generation of players are gonna succumb to these Lakers. I said what I said and I meant what I meant.”He also challenged Williams to say whether his claim about a team led by three white players winning a title was wrong. He then said he was done discussing the matter.Viewers also criticised Smith. Some said race should not be part of a debate about a team’s chances. Others accused him of raising the subject to attract attention. One fan said sports should offer an escape from daily tensions.Smith has claimed that current and former NBA players privately agree with him. Some fans doubted that, arguing players are focused on winning games rather than stopping a team because of the race of its leading players.Fans also raised past NBA champions. The 1958 St. Louis Hawks had Bob Pettit, Slater Martin and Cliff Hagan among their key players. The 1980s Boston Celtics had Larry Bird, Kevin McHale and Danny Ainge, but also had Black Hall of Famer Robert Parish. Those teams do not provide a simple answer to Smith’s argument.Smith had earlier said a Lakers championship would be good for the NBA and Los Angeles ahead of the 2028 Summer Olympics. Still, he said he could not see a team with three white leading players winning the title.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: LeBron James celebrates Savannah James’ latest milestone in her career as she opens up about her skincare brand
articles.summary: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has been married to his wife, popular entrepreneur, for close to two decades.
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has been married to his wife, popular entrepreneur, for close to two decades. While Savannah James has been there for him through all the challenges he has faced in his personal and personal life, LeBron James has now stepped up to be there for her as she achieves success in her career.LeBron James stands by his wife, Savannah James, as she achieves success with her skincare brand, Reframe BeautyA few hours ago, the Philadelphia 76ers’ star player LeBron James took to his social media to make a post about his wife, Savannah James, as she has recently sat for an interview about her successful skincare brand, Reframe Beauty.This is not the first time that the four time NBA champion have cheered on his wife, Savannah James, in public.Savannah James opens up about why she launched her skincare line as LeBron James stands by her sideIn the recent interview with Inc, LeBron James’ wife Savannah James opened up about the success of her skincare brand, Reframe Beauty, as she said, “I feel like sometimes the level of seriousness comes down to who is the face of what these brands are…I didn’t want that to be a hindrance to the efficacy of the products.”She added, “Just give me one step; I promise you it will be a game changer,” she shared. “I want you to be able to add it into your existing routine and see for yourself.”In another interview with Elle, the popular entrepreneur Savannah James opened up about why she launched a skincare line instead of a makeup line as she said, I believe that the foundation is the most important. I think that when you take care of your skin, it takes care of you. We have to protect our skin. That’s not to say that I wouldn’t extend into makeup or even hair care, but I definitely wanted to start with the basics.”The popular entrepreneur added, “It’s totally different! With Reframe, I’m putting my name and face on it and asking people to trust me with using it on their skin. It’s very nerve-racking, but I have complete faith in what we’ve created.”In many of her interviews, LeBron James’ wife Savannah James has also spoken about how the NBA icon motivated her to launch her own brand after staying out of the spotlight for years.While LeBron James’ move to the Philadelphia 76ers has sparked a debate, his wife Savannah James has spoken about how she and their daughter have preferred to live in their Los Angeles mansion as he plays for his new team.It has raised eyebrows among fans but both LeBron James and his wife, Savannah James, have stayed away from the drama.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El coloso Great Osobor ve la luz casi un año después de su terrible lesión
articles.standfirst: El pívot, que se destrozó la rodilla izquierda en su segundo partido con la selección, publica un esperanzador vídeo en el que se observan sus grandes evoluciones
articles.summary: El pívot, que se destrozó la rodilla izquierda en su segundo partido con la selección, publica un esperanzador vídeo en el que se observan sus grandes evoluciones
articles.body: Hace casi un año que Great Osobor sufrió una gravísima lesión en su segundo partido con la selección española: esguince del ligamento lateral interno de la rodilla izquierda, rotura radial del cuerno anterior del menisco externo y rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de esta misma articulación. Un diagnóstico devastador. Después de una larga y durísima recuperación, el coloso de 2,03 metros y 23 años nacido en Tudela empieza a ver la luz. En su cuenta en Instagram ha publicado un vídeo con alguna imagen de su lesión y con parte de su entrenamiento. Muchos ejercicios de fuerza para recuperar la musculatura perdida, trabajo en pista, tiro, contundentes mates... Una invitación al optimismo. "Esto sólo es un capítulo de mi historia, no el final", sentenciaba el pívot en una charla con MARCA a finales de junio. Si todo va bien, cada vez está más cerca el día en que volverá a escribir. Tras lesionarse aquel 30 de noviembre en un partido de las Ventanas FIBA ante Georgia, Osobor fue operado en Madrid por el prestigioso doctor Manuel Leyes. Después pasó seis semanas en Berlín y más tarde se trasladó a Estados Unidos, donde ha estado haciendo su recuperación. Todo bajo la supervisión de la Federación Española de Baloncesto con Elena Isla, directora del Área Médica, al frente. El seleccionador Chus Mateo también ha estado pendiente de su evolución. "Es muy importante para mí que estén pendientes. Me mandan mensajes, hablamos y eso me motiva para seguir trabajando todos los días", contaba. "No hay plazos", decía entonces. Más de cuatro meses después, las imágenes publicadas en sus redes sociales muestran una evolución muy positiva, pero él sigue yendo con calma. "In no rush" ("sin prisa"), escribió junto al vídeo. También sin pausa, con el regreso como objetivo y el sueño de poder jugar de nuevo con la selección. Su contrato con el Science City Jena alemán, su primer equipo profesional tras dejar la NCAA, finalizó el 30 de junio. La temporada pasada promediaba 16,1 puntos, 4,3 rebotes y 1,7 recuperaciones hasta que se lesionó. Cuando esté totalmente recuperado tendrá que encontrar un destino. "Lo más importante sería jugar en una situación que me ayudé a seguir creciendo como jugador y como persona. Si el próximo destino es en la ACB, me encantaría", dejaba caer quien, pese a ser tudelano, no contaría como cupo: "No tengo claro cómo funciona, pero a veces hay situaciones especiales. Yo nací en España".

articles.title: "I'm just disappointed": Is the news of LeBron James expressing disappointment in GTA 6 true amid his impressive performance?
articles.summary: LeBron James, the 41 year old NBA icon, has remained focused on his career while playing for the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body: LeBron James, the 41 year old NBA icon, has remained focused on his career while playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. While he has recorded a pretty impressive performance in the ongoing season, LeBron James has been dragged into GTA 6 drama.Has LeBron James expressed disappointment in GTA 6 amid its record breaking release?No, the four time NBA champion, LeBron James has not made any comments about the release of GTA 6 yet.In the last few hours, various parody pages have made fake posts about LeBron James’ alleged comments about GTA 6 when he has remained silent about it.A parody page on X made a post that read as, “LeBron James On GTA 6—Says He is Disappointed: "Honestly, man, I’m just disappointed. You got millions of people….myself included…..who waited 13 years for this game expecting something way more sophisticated, with next-level, groundbreaking graphics. To make the fans wait over a decade, charge $100 for the base game, and then come out with basic graphics?”The fake post added, “That’s crazy to me. It feels like they got lazy because they knew people were gonna buy it off the name alone. Look at what other studios are doing right now, and then you look at this …..it looks like a glorified DLC from 2013. When you’re at the top, there’s a standard you gotta uphold, and right now, Rockstar is coasting off legacy instead of delivering greatness. Fans deserve way better than a cash grab."Despite the post being completely made up, many fans have already believed it.A fan commented, “He’s absolutely right! GTA 6 is the biggest scam—making players wait 10 years just to be disappointed!”Another fan wrote, “Lebron is saying this!!! This should tell u all something about GTA.”However, the 41 year old four time NBA champion LeBron James has not addressed the fake rumors related to him yet.Interestingly, in 2023, LeBron James had taken to his social media to comment on an early GTA 6 trailer as his post on X read as, "GTA 6 looks INSANE!!!! SHEESH".While it has been rumored that LeBron James is a fan of Grand Theft Auto, he has never made any remarks about it in public except for a post on the trailer.LeBron James records an impressive performance even at 41 years oldFor now, all eyes remain on LeBron James’ performance in the new season as he remains a force to be reckoned with on the court.In the 2026–27 NBA regular season, LeBron James is averaging 15.7 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 6.8 assists in 32.5 minutes per game across 12 appearances for the Philadelphia 76ers.In a recent post game interview, the star player complimented teammate Labaron Philon Jr. as he said, "He's our first-round draft pick. He's not a guy that's afraid of the moment as well…When his number was called, he came in and gave us some big-time minutes and big-time shots. He was big time in his minutes."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 3 months after retirement, 9-time NBA All-Star makes heartwarming Thanksgiving gesture through his Why Not foundation
articles.summary: Russell Westbrook spent Thursday in the rain at Jesse Owens Park, the South Los Angeles park where he grew up, handing out Thanksgiving meals and
articles.body: Russell Westbrook spent Thursday in the rain at Jesse Owens Park, the South Los Angeles park where he grew up, handing out Thanksgiving meals and groceries. It was the 14th annual giveaway from the Why Not? Foundation and the largest yet, with 1,500 families receiving holiday dinners and winter coats. The event came three months after the nine-time All-Star retired from the NBA, ending 18 seasons across seven teams, the last with the Sacramento Kings. Video shared by NBA reporter Joey Linn shows Westbrook loading food packages next to volunteers, even as the rain kept coming.Russell Westbrook’s giveaway grows to 1,500 familiesVolunteers packed the supplies Tuesday at It’s Bigger Than Us in Baldwin Hills Crenshaw Plaza, with backing from LA County Parks and Recreation, Los Angeles County and Cal Dental USA. By Thursday, the handout moved to the park, and Westbrook was there with family members, staff and volunteers.The bigger budget came from September, when the sixth annual Why Not? Poker Night in Las Vegas raised more than $900,500. Six years of the event now add up to nearly $3 million.The giveaway started at the park 14 years ago, and the foundation has shown up every November since, Westbrook said. “This is home.” With more to work with this year, the plan was easy: “why not give more back to the community?”For families picking up food and coats, the help can ease the cost of Thanksgiving dinner and winter gear.The park where Westbrook grew up and the court named for himLinn pointed to the park’s history in his post. Three years ago, Westbrook and the Clippers opened a community court there.The Clippers Foundation and LA County Parks marked the November 2023 opening, when the main court became the Russell Westbrook Community Court. The ceremony also completed 117 renovated Clippers Community Courts across LA County. Earlier that day, Why Not? gave out 1,000 Thanksgiving meals to families in need.Westbrook grew emotional that day while recalling basketball games at the park in football cleats, before heading back to the football field.The work is not new to Westbrook, who often did community work even while still playing.The career line ended at 20.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 8.0 assists and 1.6 steals per game. The résumé includes the 2017 MVP award, two scoring titles, three assists titles, nine All-NBA selections, an Olympic gold medal and the all-time triple-double record. Oklahoma City fans have their own history with Westbrook from the Thunder years, and the bond has outlasted the playing days there.Why Not? was founded in 2012 and works across community assistance, education, sports, youth development and mental health.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Is Jalen Brunson alright? Knicks’ star exits Timberwolves game following injury scare
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson left Thursday night’s game against the Minnesota Timberwolves early in the first quarter after taking a hit to the face from LaMelo Ball at
articles.body: Jalen Brunson left Thursday night’s game against the Minnesota Timberwolves early in the first quarter after taking a hit to the face from LaMelo Ball at Target Center. The Knicks guard went to the locker room with 9:19 left in the period and New York trailing 7-2. Brunson had not scored in his first three minutes. No diagnosis had been announced, and there was no word on a return. The scare came on the road after back-to-back wins over the Toronto Raptors, and New York was looking to extend its winning streak against one of the West’s better teams.What happened to Brunson against the Timberwolves?Jalen Brunson took the contact on a LaMelo Ball drive, less than three minutes into the game. He did not stay on the bench. The guard went inside for evaluation, and coach Mike Brown had to rework his rotation sooner than planned.Brunson had already come through one close call earlier in the week. In Tuesday’s 111-102 win at Toronto, he scored 31 points and appeared to twist an ankle on a four-point play late in the game. He recovered and New York finished the night on a 9-0 run. Before that, he hit a clutch basket in a 112-108 overtime win over the same Raptors.He came in averaging 27 points and 5.9 assists a game and had a central role in both Toronto wins. The Knicks lean on him to set up the offense and to manufacture shots when plays stall, so an early exit on the road is a real concern.Knicks lineup options if Brunson is outIf Brunson cannot return, Brown has a few places to turn. Jose Alvarado is an experienced point guard option, and Miles McBride can take extra minutes in the backcourt. Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby could be asked to carry more of the scoring. No one on that list gives the Knicks what Brunson does, both as a scorer and as the player who makes the calls, which is why losing him, even for a stretch, would be hard to cover.Minnesota is not the easiest place to test that depth. The Timberwolves came in at 11-4 even without injured star Anthony Edwards. Ball has taken on more of the offense in that absence, giving the Wolves another creator in the backcourt.The night was also a homecoming for Towns, who spent nine seasons in Minnesota before joining New York. Brunson’s early exit pulled the attention away from that storyline. For the moment, the Knicks were waiting on an update about whether their floor leader would get back on the court.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns’ father plays surprise role as Knicks star extends remarkable record-breaking streak
articles.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns had a helping hand from an unexpected place in the Knicks’ 102-99 win over the Timberwolves on Thursday night.
articles.body: Karl-Anthony Towns had a helping hand from an unexpected place in the Knicks’ 102-99 win over the Timberwolves on Thursday night. His father, Karl Towns Sr., pulled him off the floor after an and-1 finish in the first quarter at Target Center in Minneapolis. The 31-year-old big man went on to score 22 points with 12 rebounds. It was the 15th straight double-double to open the season, a new franchise record. New York improved to 9-6 and has won three in a row. Only three points separated the teams at the final buzzer.Why did Karl Towns Sr. help Karl-Anthony Towns off the floor?Karl-Anthony Towns attacked the rim in the first quarter, finished through contact and drew the foul. He hit the floor on the play, and Karl Towns Sr. was close enough to reach down and help him up. The two shared a quick celebration at courtside, and cameras caught it. A clip of the moment was posted on social media.Towns went right at Minnesota inside the paint from the start. The Timberwolves are one of the better teams in the Western Conference, and the and-1 came early. Towns is in a third season with the Knicks and has played in the NBA since 2015. Target Center is an old stomping ground for him, and a family member was right there to see the win.Towns sets a Knicks record with 15 straight double-doublesTowns finished with 22 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and three blocks in 32 minutes. He made 9 of 20 shots and 2 of 8 from three, the one soft spot in the line. The rest sits close to the season averages of 21.2 points, 14.1 rebounds and 3.9 assists he took into the game.The Knicks have played 15 games, and Towns has a double-double in every one of them. Rebounding is the biggest piece of what he gives New York on defense. He is not a defensive anchor in the classic sense, but the three blocks helped.Jalen Brunson had an injury scare early, then finished with 21 points and seven assists. articles.title: Damian Lillard scores season-high 33 points in first game vs. Bucks post-injury, leads Trail Blazers to win
articles.summary: Lillard's 33 points were a season high and his most since March 5, 2025.
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers made the trek to Milwaukee last year to play the Bucks. Damian Lillard was present, even though he was sitting out the entire 2025-26 campaign — his first season back with the Trail Blazers — as he recovered from the Achilles tear he suffered while playing for the Bucks in their 2025 first-round playoff series .

Fiserv Forum aired a video tribute to Lillard amid that November 2025 meeting, and the nine-time All-Star received a standing ovation after it played that night.

Thursday marked the 36-year-old guard's first time taking the court against Milwaukee since his injury and his two-season stint with the Bucks. Lillard was subdued talking about the matchup in the lead-up to tip-off , but he came away with his best performance in 624 days.

March 5, 2025, was the last time Lillard had a 30-point game. He scored a season-high 33 points on Thursday in a 124-114 victory over a reeling and rebuilding Milwaukee (1-15).

Portland (10-5) bounced back after dropping consecutive games to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

So, on Thursday, Milwaukee fans watched their team lose its 12th straight game and Lillard shoot 10 of 18 from the field, including 5 of 12 from the beyond the arc.

Plus, another former Bucks player, Jrue Holiday — part of Milwaukee's NBA championship team in 2020-21 — put on a show of his own. He logged 22 points, 7 assists and 4 steals.

Holiday stepped back to hit a crucial jumper with about 5 ½ minutes to go. Another 36-year-old guard, Holiday went on to help the Trail Blazers create separation late, even coupling a steal with a layup .

Portland also got 27 points and seven rebounds from a much younger member of its backcourt: Scoot Henderson.

Milwaukee had four players score 15-plus points this time out. Tyler Herro led the way with 19, Kasparas Jakučionis and Nate Ament had 18 apiece and Ryan Rollins chipped in 15. Turner, notably, was out with a shoulder injury .

The lead changed hands incessantly on Thursday. Herro drew the Bucks within one at the 3:18 mark in the fourth quarter. The Trail Blazers, though, scored the final nine points, with Lillard netting the last two at the free-throw line.

articles.body: Tari Eason's dispute with his former girlfriend has taken another legal turn, with the Houston Rockets forward now seeking financial compensation over a collection of allegedly stolen luxury belongings. The 25-year-old NBA player claims the fallout from their relationship cost him expensive designer clothing, accessories and other valuables. The latest court action adds a financial dimension to a dispute that had already reached the courts over allegations of physical violence and property damage.Eason is now seeking to recover what he says he lost.What is Tari Eason seeking in the lawsuit against his ex-girlfriend?Tari Eason, the $81.5 million Rockets forward, is seeking compensation after accusing his former girlfriend, Marilyn Maritza Melo Rodriguez, of taking several luxury possessions from his rental property in June. According to the court filing, via TMZ, Eason alleges Rodriguez entered the property without permission, damaged his clothes with bleach and took expensive personal belongings.The list includes a $15,000 Louis Vuitton duffel bag, a Rolex watch, Chrome Hearts glasses and other valuables. Eason claims his former girlfriend has refused to return the items despite repeated requests from him and his attorney.The financial claim goes beyond the missing accessories. Eason estimates his total losses, including the damaged clothing, at no less than $92,000. He is seeking up to three times the amount in damages under California law, along with additional compensation and legal fees.The lawsuit puts a specific financial figure on the dispute. It also gives Eason another legal avenue to address property he claims was damaged or taken during the relationship fallout.How does the lawsuit connect to Eason's earlier restraining order?The latest filing follows a domestic violence restraining order request Eason made in July. In his earlier petition, the Rockets forward alleged Rodriguez punched him repeatedly in the face following an argument. He also claimed she damaged thousands of dollars' worth of his designer clothing by pouring bleach on it.Eason further alleged threats against his safety, claiming one of Rodriguez's friends contacted him and said she would "break both of my legs" and "kill me."He asked the court to restrict Rodriguez from approaching him, his home, workplace, vehicle and other locations. A judge granted a temporary restraining order, which also covered NBA facilities where Eason might play or practice.However, the allegations have been disputed. A source close to Rodriguez previously told TMZ her account was false and misleading, maintaining the reports did not accurately reflect her experience.The temporary restraining order is still in effect, with a hearing scheduled for July 29, 2027.For Eason, the latest lawsuit is about recovering property and seeking financial damages, while the earlier court action concerns his personal safety. articles.title: No. 8 Houston holds on to win Players Era 8 championship despite Tyran Stokes-led push from No. 11 Kansas
articles.summary: The Cougars were up by as many as 24 points in the first half, but a furious comeback bid from the Jayhawks made it a 4-point game with 2:34 remaining.
articles.body:
Tyran Stokes, the Rivals industry ranking's No. 1 recruit in the 2026 class and a top NBA Draft prospect, took over in the second half Thursday night in the Players Era 8 championship at Las Vegas' Michelob ULTRA Arena.

Stokes fueled a head-turning comeback bid after No. 11 Kansas trailed No. 8 Houston by as many as 24 points in the first half.

The Jayhawks pulled within four points of the Cougars with a bit more than 2 ½ minutes remaining. Then Houston responded with an 8-0 run that effectively clinched what turned out to be a 92-83 victory .

Both teams were playing their third game in three days to cap the early-season tournament. The Cougars (6-0) came out on top and demonstrated that they're capable of winning a much more prestigious tourney in the spring. Kansas (5-1) will regroup and get another crack at the Cougars in Big 12 play on Feb. 1.

Earlier in the night, top-ranked Florida, which lost to Houston on Wednesday , won the Players Era 8 tournament's third-place game, defeating West Virginia 85-72 .

While Stokes picked up a couple early personals and navigated foul trouble down the stretch, the freshman guard finished with 22 points and 11 rebounds, logging his third consecutive double-double. His intensity went a long way in igniting the Jayhawks' surge, as he accounted for 15 points and eight boards in the second half alone.

Kansas also got 18 points from senior guard Dennis Parker Jr. and 17 from sophomore guard Leroy Blyden Jr. Those two went a combined 22 of 23 from the charity stripe.

Houston was paced by junior guard Mercy Miller. He clocked out with 21 points, 8 rebounds and 4 assists, connecting on four 3-pointers in the process. Senior forward Delrecco Gillespie wasn't far behind with 19 points and seven boards. Dedan Thomas Jr. came through in the clutch, warding off Kansas late. The senior guard paired a layup and jumper to give Houston breathing room after the Jayhawks were on the brink of making it one-possession game.

The Cougars dominated the opening 20 minutes of play Thursday. They scored 11 straight points while Kansas went more than four minutes without one.

After that, Kelvin Sampson's squad was ahead 15-3. Houston came in averaging 5.2 triples per game and had four of them less than eight minutes in. The Cougars simultaneously sped up and beat up the Jayhawks.

By intermission, Houston was up to 54 points, tied for the most Kansas has allowed in a first half under Bill Self, who's been at the helm since 2003-04.

Known for their physicality, the Cougars imposed their will on both ends of the floor in that opening period. Not only did their defense make things difficult for the Jayhawks, but their offense was unrelenting as well.

Houston doubled up Kansas in paint points 24-12 in the first half and outscored the Jayhawks in second-chance points 18-3 along the way.

Self's group punched back following halftime.

At the end of a 12-0 Kansas run, Stokes went coast-to-coast, slammed on the brakes and scored inside.

Later, he snagged a steal that ultimately led to a Blyden 3-pointer. In that same stretch, amid a 10-0 Jayhawks run, Stokes challenged a pass, resulting in a Houston turnover.

His valiant effort, as well as the one put forth by the Jayhawks as a whole, simply fell short. It would have been historic had they came back.

AP top-10 teams in the last 30 seasons, according to the ESPN broadcast, were 1,224-0 when leading by 20-plus points at halftime.

Houston didn't end up being the outlier.

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg breaks silence on losing streak with honest admission that raises bigger questions
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg is not hiding how much the Warriors’ five-game slide hurts.
articles.body: Yaxel Lendeborg is not hiding how much the Warriors’ five-game slide hurts. The rookie scored 11 points on 3-of-11 shooting in Thursday’s 126-98 loss to Memphis, which dropped Golden State to 8-9 and ended a winless road trip. Stephen Curry has been out with an oblique injury since the trip opened. Golden State had won eight straight before it all turned. Lendeborg has now spoken about how he is handling it, including the words Draymond Green offered after the New Orleans loss and the story behind a haircut that drew attention.What did Yaxel Lendeborg say about the Warriors’ losing streak?Lendeborg opened with a simple line: “I hate losing, man.” He went on to explain that he has never dropped this many games this early. A year ago he lost three times. The season before, he said he could not even recall the number. Now he feels he is letting his teammates down, and the numbers have not helped. Lendeborg cited a 9-for-23 shooting night as an example, calling that kind of inefficiency awful and saying it makes the sting worse.The frustration showed during Monday’s loss to the Pelicans. Lendeborg sat on the bench for several minutes in the fourth quarter with a towel over his head, and teammates and coaches noticed.The drop is sharp. Two weeks ago, the 24-year-old rookie was scoring 37 and setting franchise records. On Thursday, he finished with 11 points, eight rebounds and seven assists in about 33 minutes, making three of 11 shots. He added two blocks and a steal but also turned the ball over three times. Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer, the third overall pick, went 6-for-6 for 16 points in the same game. Entering the game, the NBA had pointed out that Boozer and Lendeborg were the first pair of rookies since Larry Bird and Magic Johnson in 1979-80 to average at least 16 points, seven rebounds and three assists through 15 games.Green’s blunt advice and the haircut timingGreen pulled the rookie aside after the Pelicans game with a direct message. According to Lendeborg, the veteran told him to stop showing so much weakness, because an opponent who sees it will go at him. Lendeborg took it as a call to fix his mental side of the game.The advice arrives with the team at 8-9, a long way from the eight-game winning streak the rookie helped power not long ago.The haircut got its own explanation. Lendeborg said it looked like a reaction to the Spurs loss, but the idea had been building for a while. He wanted a restart, and he admitted the timing made it seem like something it was not.Golden State now heads home and waits on Curry, who tore his oblique in the first quarter against Houston on Nov. 11. articles.title: Nate Ament scores career high in second NBA start
articles.summary: Nate Ament records a career high for points and rebounds in his second NBA start.
articles.body:
Portland (10-5) defeated Milwaukee (1-15), 124-114, on Thursday at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. 13,545 were in attendance for the NBA game .

Former Vol Nate Ament made his second career start for the Bucks. He recorded career highs for points (18) and rebounds (nine) in 35 minutes. Ament converted 6-of-11 field goal attempts, 2-of-5 three-point attempts and 2-of-5 free throw attempts. He also totaled nine rebounds (six defensive).

Tyler Herro led Milwaukee in scoring with 19 points in 31 minutes. He converted 7-of-13 field goal attempts, 4-of-7 three-point attempts and 1-of-3 free throw attempts.

Portland guard Damian Lillard led all scorers with 33 points.

The Trail Blazers led for 60% of the contest. Portland's largest lead was 12 points. Milwaukee's largest lead was eight points.

The Bucks' 1-15 record is the worst start through their first 16 games of a season in franchise history.

articles.title: New Dejounte Murray Trade Rumors on Suns Doing 'Background Work' amid Jalen Green Links
articles.summary: With Dejounte Murray seeking a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, the Phoenix Suns' need for a point guard has them starting to gather some information about the former All-Star.
articles.body:
With Dejounte Murray seeking a trade from the New Orleans Pelicans, the Phoenix Suns' need for a point guard has them starting to gather some information about the former All-Star.

On the latest episode of The Hoop Collective Podcast (starts at 47:30 mark), ESPN's Brian Windhorst revealed the Suns have made calls to do exploratory "background work" on Murray.

The Athletic's Sam Amick added there is "zero traction" in any talks between the Suns and Pelicans.

"As it stands, though, team sources on both sides, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, say nothing even remotely close to a deal is happening," Amick reported Friday. "Those team sources say there was a brief recent discussion between the two teams — five minutes in all — but zero traction in the talks."

The Pelicans announced on Nov. 13 that Murray requested a trade and they would "evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization."

One issue for Murray is his value around the NBA right now doesn't seem particularly high as his performance has declined and his contract pays him $32.8 million this season with a $30.8 million player option for 2027-28.

Phoenix is in a similar situation with Jalen Green, whose value is way down amid his early-season struggles. He is owed $36.3 million this season and has a $36 million player option for next season.

Green has been cited as a potential trade candidate for the Suns in their quest to add a point guard.

Windhorst said earlier in the week that multiple teams view Murray as a "distressed asset" that would require the Pelicans to attach something to the deal for a team to take his contract.

There's no indication the Suns are close to a trade for Murray, but their need for help at point guard would make him a potential fit.

Devin Booker has been the primary ballhandler in Phoenix this season. He leads the team in scoring average (24.8 points per game) and assists (5.4), but his best seasons have come playing with a traditional point guard.

Murray is averaging just 13.4 points on 43.1 percent shooting (29.6 percent from three) and 4.4 assists per game in nine starts for the Pelicans this season. He's on pace for his lowest scoring average and fewest assists since the 2019-20 campaign.

The Suns (7-7) have won six of their last eight games following a 1-5 start. They are currently 11th in the Western Conference standings.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama, NBA's dunk king, turns to the 'shunk' due to painful blister on hand
articles.summary: Wembanyama is on pace to set the NBA record for dunks in a season.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has found a new way to shoot in order to give his hands a rest and prevent future blisters.

It's called the "shunk," as San Antonio Spurs color commentator Sean Elliott put it. It's basically the 7-foot-4 Wembanyama "dunking" the ball through the basket like a jump shot.

Wembanyama showed off the "shunk" during the Spurs' 124-112 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. The two-time All-Star posted 32 points, 11 rebounds and 1 "shunk."

"I'm not going to lie," Wembanyama said afterward via ESPN . "Actually, I've had this blister forever, and it's killing me. And every time I dunk, it kills me. I've been dragging this blister for I don't know how long because of dunking. So, I did not [quit dunking], but if I can avoid it, I would."

Through 16 games, Wembanyama leads all players with 72 dunks — Thursday's "shunk" was counted as a dunk by the NBA. The next closest is Giannis Antetokounmpo of the Miami Heat, who has 49. The Spurs star is on pace for 369 dunks this season, which would pass Rudy Gobert's record of 306 he amassed during the 2018-19 season.

Was the "shunk" the shortest jump shot Wembanyama has ever attempted?

"Yeah, for sure," he said. "Maybe ever."

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Reveals If She Thinks JuJu Watkins Should Enter WNBA Draft or Stay in WCBB
articles.summary: While USC guard JuJu Watkins will likely be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 WNBA draft if she declares, Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham expressed her belief Thursday that Watkins should stay in school for another year.
articles.body:
While USC guard JuJu Watkins will likely be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 WNBA draft if she declares, Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham expressed her belief Thursday that Watkins should stay in school for another year.

Speaking on her No Hesitation podcast (beginning at the 38-minute mark) , Cunningham said, "If I was in her shoes, I think a lot of people are going to stay in college. Like, why would you not go and collect all that money that you can? ... I would stay in college personally. I'm going to go get that money, Just enjoy where your two feet are at."

Cunningham's comments came after her co-host, Drew Hanlen, broke down Watkins' financial situation and how it would change if she were to make the jump to the WNBA.

Hanlen noted that it is believed Watkins is currently making between $750,000 and $1 million to play at USC, whereas her rookie contract would only be worth $565,000 as the No. 1 overall pick in the WNBA draft.

The Toronto Tempo won the 2027 WNBA draft lottery, making them the likely landing spot for Watkins should she declare.

Before offering the advice of staying in college, Cunningham made sure to praise the Tempo organization and the city of Toronto, expressing her belief that Watkins would love to play there.

Still, Cunningham came to the conclusion that Watkins should maximize her earning potential by spending another season in the college ranks.

The 2025 Naismith and Associated Press College Player of the Year, the 21-year-old Watkins is off to a hot start once again this season for the No. 4 Trojans, averaging 24.5 points, 6.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game.

While she would undoubtedly have a chance to become the WNBA's next big star, Watkins' financial ceiling would almost certainly be far greater in the NCAA next season since USC and other top schools would likely bid for her services.

articles.title: NBA Scout Says AJ Dybantsa Landed In 'Tough Environment,' Rips Wizards' Culture
articles.summary: Amid an uneven start to his NBA career, some people in the know gave their thoughts this week on rookie No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa's situation with the Washington Wizards.
articles.body:
Amid an uneven start to his NBA career, some people in the know gave their thoughts this week on rookie No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa's situation with the Washington Wizards.

Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst , an anonymous Eastern Conference scout said, "He's in a tough environment for a rookie. There's not a high level of accountability there for their top players and so there isn't down the line."

The Wizards have not reached the playoffs since 2021, and they are in the midst of their third season under head coach Brian Keefe.

Washington went 18-64 in 2024-25 and 17-65 in 2025-26, but there was hope for a major improvement this season following the selection of Dybantsa and the acquisition of veteran All-Stars Anthony Davis and Trae Young.

While the Wizards are trending better than they were the past two years, they are still just 5-11 thus far, placing them 11th in the Eastern Conference.

Dybantsa, 19, is averaging 16.3 points, 6.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 steals in 33.8 minutes per game, but he is shooting just 41.6 percent from the field and 21.3 percent from beyond the arc.

An anonymous Western Conference executive suggested that Dybantsa is perhaps being held back and prevented from playing to his greatest strengths, telling Windhorst: "He's so big, so powerful and plays so much force that it demands that he have the ball and space. But it's hard with [Davis and Young] there because they are soaking up a lot of the possessions and the team is naturally going to cater to them."

Dybantsa is coming off the best game of his young NBA career, though, scoring a career-high 23 points on 9-of-17 shooting to go along with 12 rebounds in a 103-99 win over the Toronto Raptors.

Given his talent level, Dybantsa only figures to get better as the season goes on, although it is fair to wonder how well he will fit alongside Young and Davis moving forward, especially if they dominate the ball and limit his opportunities.

articles.title: NBA Insiders Sound Off on Darius Acuff Jr.'s Playing Style, 'He Needs to Realize It's a Team Game'
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr.'s overwhelming ball-dominance has been the primary talking point around the team so far this season, with people around the NBA wanting to see him evolve his game.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr.'s overwhelming ball-dominance has been the primary talking point around the team so far this season, with people around the NBA wanting to see him evolve his game.

Speaking to ESPN's Tim MacMahon , one Eastern Conference scout said "he needs to realize it's a team game" when discussing Acuff and how he needs to grow.

"He needs to realize it's a team game," the scout said. "There's no doubt he's a talent. Defensively challenged, to say the least. He can pass — he just doesn't want to pass."

The NBA Rookies Who Are Looking Like Draft Steals 🏀

On a more positive note, an Eastern Conference executive told MacMahon part of the problem is the situation around Acuff in Sacramento.

"He needs to be coached hard and coached well and develop good habits defensively," the executive said. "It's a shame he's going to waste this year with Doug Christie. But he's going to be a stud offensively for sure."

The Kings made no secret of the fact that Acuff was the player they wanted in the 2026 NBA draft. Things worked out in their favor to take him at No. 7 overall, handing him the keys to the car on offense.

Acuff has been more than happy to occupy the driver seat. He is averaging 26.2 points on 22.6 field-goal attempts per game. Luka Dončić (25.6) and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (23.3) are the only players taking more shot attempts so far this season.

There have been rumblings about potential unhappiness among Kings players, particularly Domantas Sabonis, with Acuff's shot volume. Brendan Nunes of Sactown Sports 1140 poured some cold water on that chatter, noting Acuff and Sabonis have a strong relationship.

Even with his high shot volume, Acuff is also racking up assists. He averages 7.0 dimes per game. Dončić and Cade Cunningham are the only other players averaging at least 25 points and seven assists per contest.

This isn't to suggest Acuff is anywhere close to that level right now, but the Kings won 22 games last season. They haven't been a good team for a long time, nor are they loaded with talent around Acuff right now that he needs to be deferring to.

The key is making sure Acuff doesn't maintain some of his bad tendencies going forward as the Kings try to build their roster around him.

Whether that comes from, as the executive said, tougher coaching or just learning from experience, the Kings need Acuff to become a more well-rounded player as they try to build a team that is eventually good enough to compete for a playoff spot in the Western Conference.

articles.title: NBA one-month awards! MVP, best rookie, breakout stars and surprise teams so far
articles.summary: With the NBA season hitting the one-month mark, let's hand out some early awards.
articles.body:
With the NBA season hitting the one-month mark, let's hand out some early awards! Who has been the most valuable player so far? The best rookie? The league's breakout star? Our writers weigh in with their picks.

Kelly Iko: Victor Wembanyama, with a sliiiight edge over Luka Dončić. Of players that have registered at least 300 minutes so far, the Spurs are 42.5 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor, the most impactful in the league by some distance. (San Antonio looked like a fish out of water earlier this week when he was on the bench vs. Detroit.) He's also realized that, at 7-foot-4, his rim presence should be consistently weaponized. Per Second Spectrum, Wemby logged 65 alley-oop dunk attempts all of last season; he's at 40 before Thanksgiving. Add this growth to his continued defensive wizardry, along with taking care of the ball and improving as a creator, and you have yourself a solid argument.

Steve Jones: Luka Dončić. At this check-in, I have to go with Dončić after a month full of a variety pack of stepback 3s. That's 38 points a night with defenses attempting to throw multiple schemes at him and it just hasn't mattered a ton yet. Combine that with him "doing his job" on defense, with more activity on switches and rotations; he's a big reason why the Lakers are at the top of the West.

Dan Devine: Luka Dončić. I'm with Steve, give me the league's leading scorer, the reason the Lakers have been consistently vying for the No. 1 offense in the NBA, and the driving force behind an L.A. team that couldn't get out of the first round last year being neck-and-neck with the conference champion Spurs and East-leading 76ers for the league's best record. For more information, consult your local library:

Nekias Duncan: Victor Wembanyama. I don't think you can go wrong with Dončić or Wembanyama, honestly, but 28-12-3-1-4 on 62 true shooting is absolutely nuts. Wemby's dunking everything in sight, making teams pay when they send help — his assist rate has risen, while his turnover rate has dropped from last year — and he's pretty easily been the most destructive defender in basketball this year. The "off" portion of Wemby's on-off numbers are insane, but I'd redirect to the "on" portion — the Spurs are outscoring teams by over 28 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor.

Duncan: Cameron Boozer. With all due respect to Yaxel Lendeborg and Darius Acuff Jr. (don't let them boo you, big dawg), I'll also be rolling with Mr. Boozer. I've been enamored with his processing speed and versatility all year long. He attacks or passes ahead of tilted defenses at a high level already. He's also showcased a willingness to let it fly from deep, a necessary buffer while he gets comfortable with his inside-the-arc work (he's converting 60% of his 2s over his last six games) against bigger players.

Jones: Cameron Boozer. Rookie of the Year is going to continue to heat up as this season goes on, but Boozer's versatility offensively has delivered consistent impact for the Grizzlies. His ability to playmake fits right in with their identity: he can punish switches, and he can make plays on the short roll. There has rarely been a game where he hasn't left an imprint for a Grizzlies team that just keeps winning.

Devine: Yaxel Lendeborg. I'm firmly on the record as very on-board for Boozer, who became the second-youngest player in NBA history to record a triple-double , but I'll give a shout out to Lendeborg. Yes, it's been a pretty brutal week for him, and for the Warriors as a whole, since Stephen Curry went down . But what he showed in his first dozen games as a pro was truly eye-opening. Coming out of Michigan, the book on Yaxel was that, as a 24-year-old super-duper-senior, he'd have the experience, toolkit and physical maturity to be able to immediately fill a role in the league. I'm not sure anyone saw that role being "guy who can average an efficient 20-plus a night on high usage, and help elevate a team that just about everybody thought was drawing dead." That might not last forever, especially if Steph's absence stretches. But for the first month, it was an exceedingly pleasant surprise.

Iko: Darius Acuff Jr. I'm not going to punish Acuff for being born into the Kings family. I'm also not going to magnify his low shot-making efficiency or assist-to-usage ratio in Sacramento . This kid is an absolute terror with the ball in his hands, averaging 26.2 points, 7.0 assists and 3.6 rebounds a night. In spite of Sacramento. You wanna know the list of folks to achieve benchmarks like that as a rookie? Wilt. Kareem. Jordan. Oscar Robertson. Elvin Hayes. Darius. His feel for the game, creation and scoring versatility is there — the rough edges will smoothen out as time goes on.

Most Surprising Team of the First Month …

Jones: Memphis Grizzlies. While the Sixers keep finding ways to win as they figure it out, and while the Lakers are at the top of the West, and the Wolves have stayed steady without Anthony Edwards, the Grizzlies being one game out of the top is something few saw coming. They are 8-0 on the road, which is not just the best road start in franchise history, but the longest road winning streak in franchise history. Let that sink in.

Duncan: Houston Rockets, if for no other reason than to save you all from the massive victory lap I'd like to take over the Grizzlies. It's not a surprise that the Rockets are a good team; the way they've been good is simply not what I had on the bingo card. They have the league's best offense and a top-five half-court unit to boot — a notable shift from last year (7th overall, 19th in the half-court). This largely hasn't been the Kevin Durant show; this is the second lowest scoring (21.3) and lowest shot-taking (13.3 attempts) season of his career. The growth and empowerment of Alperen Şengün and Amen Thompson, the confidence and shot-making of Jabari Smith Jr. (career-best 38.8% from 3), and the return of the steady-handed Fred VanVleet has led to a more efficient, free-flowing offense.

Iko: Houston Rockets. They have very quietly made a compelling case for being a top-5 team in the NBA. VanVleet's return has come with less control than he's accustomed to, but when you're converting shots at the highest efficiency of your career, who cares about usage rates? Smith is more confident in his in-between game and still has a knack for timely momentum-shifting splashes — as well as an unheralded five-position defensive skill set. They are second in offense and seventh in defense, don't turn the ball over, obliterate opponents on the offensive glass and still have a healthy Durant. Why couldn't they stick around until June?

Devine: Portland Trail Blazers, in part because I'm an incorrigible shill who wants to deliver a ruthless plug for the big story he just wrote on Damian Lillard , and in part because I'm not sure anybody saw Portland sitting at 10-5 with a top-10 defense heading into opening night. Micah Nori's done a sensational job, Donovan Clingan and Toumani Camara look like bona fide linchpins, Jrue Holiday is always just what the doctor ordered, and Scoot Henderson even broke out against the Bucks on Thursday. Get Ja Morant back on the court, and Portland might just have a stew goin'.

Most Disappointing Team of the First Month …

Devine: Toronto Raptors. It's not a shock to me that they are 5-10, given the myriad injuries they've suffered — most notably, obviously, getting just two games out of Kawhi Leonard before he went down with amorphous, ill-defined knee woes that, in a recent report by the great Michael Grange of Sportsnet , evoked the phrase "mystery condition." (Who could have foreseen this?!?) I do find it disappointing, though, that a team that won 46 games with the point differential of a 50-win squad and a top-seven defense last season — without Leonard — has so often looked so feckless this season … and that it's a combined 0-8 against teams with .500 or better records , getting blitzed by 11.5 points per 100 possessions against opponents with top-10 net ratings . Maybe, with better health, the Raptors will turn things around. Right now, though, even given the absence of their big-ticket offseason acquisition, they seem disappointingly unserious.

Iko: Charlotte Hornets. There's no way you could have convinced me the Hornets would be 28th in net rating a week before Thanksgiving. I know the injuries to Kon Knueppel and Coby White have delayed what should have been a smooth start. But there's just something off about them when you watch, a level of disharmony and disjointedness that shouldn't be there this early in a season. Their collapse this week on the road in L.A., a game in which they led quite comfortably by 18 points deep into the second half, was embarrassing. The erasure of Brandon Miller, who has suddenly turned into a hybrid of Monta Ellis and J.R. Smith, is also jarring. Charles Lee has quite the tall task on his hands.

Duncan: Utah Jazz, by default. Injuries have simply derailed this group. The playmaking and screening chops of Jusuf Nurkić were missing to begin the year, an underrated hit to what the Jazz want to establish. More pressing, they've had to navigate absences from Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen. It's led to an offense that has felt rudderless at times — and easy to switch against — paired with a defense that isn't good enough to hold things together. I simply didn't think this would be a three-win team a month in.

Jones: Cleveland Cavaliers. Per NBA.com, they are the No. 4 scoring team in the league (118.3), boasting the No. 5 offensive rating in the league (117.5), and it doesn't feel like it at all. For a team with this level of firepower, with the added bonus of continuity after an Eastern Conference finals run, the drink has felt flatter than usual. The Cavs likely just need a quick chat with momentum to turn things around, but I had high expectations for this group to take off or figure things out quickly. It has felt stuck in the middle to me.

Iko: Paul George. If this is intended for younger players, I apologize, but I'm in complete awe of what 36-year-old is doing right now in Boston. He's played next to Jayson Tatum for only a month, but their synergy screams of a lifelong partnership. He's still firing off eight 3s a night while converting them at the highest clip of his career; still serving as an effective secondary creator, scorer and connective tissue for MazzullaBall; and still one of the premier contest-without-fouling wings around. This was supposed to be a puzzling Celtics transaction, remember? Not acquiring a player nearing 40 who's still producing at a top-25 level . Color me shocked.

Jones: Davion Mitchell. Just the term breakout star had me in a headlock; I wanted to go with KAT, but he's already broken out, Cooper Flagg has taken a leap, Franz Wagner is scoring and playmaking, and LaMelo Ball is playing defense. I'm going with Mitchell, leaning on the breakout portion of the program. He's been dynamic in transition and in pick-and-roll, finding his way into the paint consistently. The on-ball pressure remains tremendous and he's knocking down 3s. He's been exactly what the Heat have needed.

Duncan: Cedric Coward. (Davion Mitchell is such a tremendous shout!) Coward has simply been awesome for the Grizzlies to start the year. He's shooting the leather off the ball (45.2% on 5.2 attempts from 3), the drives have more juice, the passing has perked up, and he continues to add value as an offensive rebounder. On the other end, he's putting together a legitimate All-Defense campaign while consistently taking on tough assignments. As of this writing, opposing offenses are generating under 0.8 points per possession whenever Coward defends a ball screen (0.76), a handoff (0.76), or an off-ball screen (0.55). There's a reason the Grizzlies have been nearly 15 points better per 100 possessions with him on the floor.

Devine: Holy crap, none of you guys said Ty Jerome? OK, then: Ty freaking Jerome!

There are five players in the NBA this season averaging at least 25 points and five assists per game on .600 true shooting, and Ty Jerome is the only one of them that 99% of NBA fans couldn't pick out of a lineup. (The other four: Luka, Giannis, Tyrese Maxey, Jamal Murray.) Sickos who do this for a living might have been aware that the eighth-year pro out of Virginia could be capable of this sort of production given health and opportunity, but it's certainly come as a shock to just about everybody else — including opponents of the Grizzlies who might've come into the season expecting things to be sweet only to find themselves on the business end of a steady diet of impossible floaters and 30-foot pull-up bombs. Memphis has been one of the best stories in the league this season, and its low-profile, high-octane point guard has been one of the biggest reasons why.

articles.title: NBA Cup scores, standings, and scenarios: Who can clinch and who's nearly toast?
articles.summary: The NBA Cup action returns on Nov. 20 with nine games on the schedule.
articles.body:
It's the fourth night of the NBA Cup, and for some teams who want to raise a banner, this might be their last chance to stay in the tournament.

Entering the games on Nov. 20, or "Moving Day," each group leader has two wins, while six teams are looking for their first win, including the reigning NBA Cup champions, the New York Knicks .

The night kicks off with the Charlotte Hornets , currently sporting the league's worst offense, facing the surprising Atlanta Hawks. articles.title: Brandon Ingram Reportedly Set to Make Clippers Debut After Achilles Injury Recovery
articles.summary: Brandon Ingram is reportedly days away from making his debut for the Los Angeles Clippers.
articles.body:
Brandon Ingram is reportedly days away from making his debut for the Los Angeles Clippers.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Friday Ingram is expected to return Monday against the Houston Rockets after sitting out the start of the season amid his recovery from Achilles and heel injuries .

The Clippers acquired Ingram from the Toronto Raptors when the Kawhi Leonard trade was finalized in September.

Ingram is coming off a lone season with the Raptors during which he earned a second career All-Star nod while averaging 21.5 points in 77 games.

He was then limited to 12 points across five playoff games before a heel injury sidelined him for the end of the Raptors' first-round loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Raptors interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden said in September Ingram had undergone heel surgery in May that also revealed a partially torn Achilles tendon.

Redden said at the time Ingram was expected to need about six months of rehab from the procedure.

Ingram said as Nov. 6 he had returned to practice, including some 5-on-5 work, and was planning on "coming back soon," per ClutchPoints' Tomas Azarly .

The Clippers currently sit 13th in the West after a 4-10 start to the team's first season without Leonard, who played just two games for the Raptors before he was sidelined with a left knee injury.

Although Bradley Beal and Jordan Miller are still sidelined indefinitely by their respective injuries, the Clippers took one step closer to a healthy lineup when backup center Yanic Konan Niederhauser made his season debut Thursday after recovering from right foot surgery.

The Clippers could hope adding Ingram to the lineup will help take some pressure off Darius Garland, who is currently leading the team with 21.3 points per game while playing more than 33 minutes per night.

Garland will be tasked with taking on that heavy workload for at least one more game as the team prepares to play Saturday at the Dallas Mavericks prior to Ingram's potential season debut Monday in Houston.

articles.title: El campeón le mete una paliza al Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, con una defensa interior lamentable y lastrados por las pérdidas, firman su peor anotación de la temporada, llegan a perder por 26 y enlazan dos dolorosas derrotas
articles.summary: Los blancos, con una defensa interior lamentable y lastrados por las pérdidas, firman su peor anotación de la temporada, llegan a perder por 26 y enlazan dos dolorosas derrotas
articles.body: La gira por el Este, con visitas al Besiktas y al Olympiacos, deja al Real Madrid hecho unos zorros. Si la derrota en Estambul ya fue dolorosa, la sufrida en Atenas resultó humillante por momentos (92-76). En la reedición de las dos últimas finales continentales, las de Euroliga y Supercup con un triunfo por bando, los griegos aplastaron a un conjunto blanco sin energía, sin defensa y sin acierto. Es como si las piernas pesaran de repente una tonelada y ahora sí que se acusan las bajas, especialmente la de Campazzo. El regreso de Maledon se notó sólo el primer día. Sumó 17 puntos y siete asistencias sin incidencia. El reestreno de Eli Ndiaye, apenas tuvo peso. No era el mejor día para volver. Fue un meneo muy serio el que se llevó el Madrid, que firmó su anotación más baja del curso, empeorando los 77 puntos que metió en Dubái. Le penalizaron de nuevo las pérdidas (17) y, sobre todo, una defensa horrible, especialmente por dentro, que permitió al Olympiacos campar a sus anchas: 28 asistencias y 26/43 en tiros de dos (60,5%). Si no batió el récord de mates de la Euroliga, debió de faltar poco. Hall (11 puntos) y Tyrique Jones (22+8) y un poco de Mbaye Ndiaye compensaron con creces la baja de Milutinov. Fournier, el MVP de la Final Four, puso el acierto exterior (17) y Vezenkov no tuvo que emplearse a fondo (14). Del lesionado Jean Montero o el apartado Dorsey no se acordó nadie. Esas ausencias son un agravante para la paliza de los blancos, que hicieron su peor partido de la temporada. La puesta en escena del Madrid ya fue dantesca, como una prolongación del partido de hacía 48 horas ante el Besiktas. O incluso peor. A los tres minutos ya acumulaba siete pérdidas, varios airballs y una técnica a Pedro Martínez. Vezenkov empezaba a hacer de las suyas (16-7) y Eli Ndiaye se reestrenaba con los blancos y se cargó rápido de faltas. Damian Jones (10+11 pero 0/5 en triples) fue de lo poco salvable del primer cuarto y del partido, aunque le penalizaron sus despistes en defensa. Tavares, con dos puntos y cuatro rebotes, ha tenido pocos partidos en los que pasara tan desapercibido. En el segundo cuarto, el Olympiacos fue un rodillo por dentro. Hall y Jones abusaron. “No canastas fáciles”, gritó Pedro Martínez en un tiempo muerto. Las dos siguientes acciones fueron mates griegos. Algunos llegaron después de pases sin mirar y hasta de espaldas, como uno extraordinario de Vezenkov. Hasta 15 asistencias locales al intermedio. El campeón jugaba a placer ante los groseros errores defensivos de su rival y la renta se iba a los 18 (47-29). Feliz, con dos tiros libres y una contra, recortó a falta de dos segundos para el descanso. Antes de ir al vestuario, Tyrique Jones anotó un triple sobre la bocina y desde medio campo. En 111 partidos en Euroliga, nunca había lanzado un triple. Todo lo que podía salirle mal al Madrid, le salía (50-33). Apilaba 12 pérdidas y de nada le servía gana el rebote con 10 ofensivos. Nada cambió a la vuelta. Jones se colgó otras dos veces del aro tras sendos pick and roll, caían dos triples y más errores en alguna puerta atrás y terribles balances defensivos. El Madrid había conseguido controlar las pérdidas, pero todo lo demás seguía bajo mínimos, en especial su defensa, que era penosa. Normal que la renta se fuera a los 24 con más de un cuarto por jugarse (73-49). La última posesión del tercer acto, con Nick Smith Jr. botando y botando ante tres rivales distintos sin llegar a tirar, fue una metáfora del partido. En un último periodo de minutos de la basura, el Madrid llegó a estar 26 puntos abajo: 83-57 a cinco minutos del final. Logró poner un poco de maquillaje a su amoratado rostro con tres triples seguidos de Okeke y recortar hasta dejar la renta en -16 tras una tarde de mucho dolor. En los dos últimos partidos, 20 puntos menos de media y una malísima imagen. Habrá que comprobar si hay efectos secundarios. 92 - Olympiacos (19+31+23+19): Joseph (3), Ward (10), Vezenkov (14), Fournier (17), Tyrique Jones (22) -cinco inicial- Miller-Mcintyre (5), Papanikolau (2), Netzipoglou (2), Hall (11), Mbaye Ndiaye (6), Plotas (-). 76 - Real Madrid (14+19+19+24): Maledon (17), Feliz (6), Procida (3), Pradilla (6), Tavares (2) -cinco inicial-, Smith Jr. (2), Damian Jones (10), Eli John Ndiaye (3), Luwawu-Cabarrot (7), Abalde (5), Okeke (12) y Llull (3). Árbitros: Ilija Belosevic (Serbia), Mehdi Difallah (Francia) y Luka Kardum (Croacia). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido de la jornada 13 de la Euroliga disputado en el Sunel Arena de Ano Liosia.
