articles.title: Tom Thibodeau's Stance on Return to Coaching Updated in New NBA Rumors amid Kings Buzz
articles.summary: Tom Thibodeau's name has been floated as a coaching candidate for NBA teams looking to make a change, but he has "made it clear that he will not be communicating with any organizations preemptively," The Athletic's Sam Amick reported on Friday.
articles.body:
Tom Thibodeau's name has been floated as a coaching candidate for NBA teams looking to make a change, but he has "made it clear that he will not be communicating with any organizations preemptively," The Athletic's Sam Amick reported on Friday.

In other words, Thibodeau does not want to privately discuss taking another coach's job while that coach still occupies the position. That could make it difficult for any team executives who might be interested in hiring the 68-year-old coach, especially since they would need to fire their current coach before finding out if Thibodeau would even be interested in joining them.

"In general, though, Thibodeau is known to be interested in returning as a head coach whenever the right opportunity presents itself," Amick wrote.

The Sacramento Kings have been named as a potential landing spot for Thibodeau after starting the season with a 1-13 record. Sacramento is heading toward its third losing season under coach Doug Christie, who wasn't able to eclipse 30 wins in either of his first two seasons as head coach.

Thibodeau could bring a lot of much-needed stability and experience to Sacramento. The two-time Coach of the Year has a .579 career winning percentage, and he only had three losing seasons in his 13 years as a head coach.

Thibodeau hasn't been on the sidelines since he was fired by the New York Knicks after the 2024-25 season. He led the Knicks to their first Eastern Conference finals appearance in a quarter century, but the team moved on from him after the Indiana Pacers eliminated New York to advance to the 2025 NBA Finals. He was succeeded by coach Mike Brown, who led the Knicks to a NBA championship.

articles.title: Colorado Rockies acquire RHP Chase Lee, DFA Jimmy Herget
articles.summary: The Rockies appear to have added a new funky-delivery pitcher to their roster.
articles.body:
The Colorado Rockies announced this afternoon that they have acquired RHP Chase Lee from the Toronto Blue Jays. In a corresponding move, RHP Jimmy Hergert has been designated for assignment.

Yesterday, Lee was designated for assignment by the Blue Jays to make space for infielder Christian Cairo.

Fitting with the Rockies' commitment to finding a variety of arm angles and approaches, Lee is a side-arm right-hander. The 28-year-old came to the Blue Jays from the Detroit Tigers during the last offseason. Lee saw limited action, pitching just 9.2 innings with the Blue Jays, where he allowed seven earned runs.

He saw more success in Triple-A Buffalo, pitching 53.2 innings with a solid 2.01 ERA. He posted a 21.8% strikeout rate and a 9.3% walk rate, both fairly average, with a 47.9% groundball rate, which is slightly above average. Lee earned a 3.80 FIP.

As an interesting note, the native of McCalla, Alabama, enrolled at the University of Alabama and tried out for their baseball team. However, he failed to make the cut. Alabama head coach Brad Bohannon suggested Lee change his pitching motion to a sidearm delivery, which was successful. The following season, he was a walk-on addition to the Crimson Tide. It was the beginning of a successful NCAA career.

He was drafted by the Texas Rangers in the sixth round of the 2021 MLB Draft and traded to Detroit in July 2024.

As for Jimmy Herget, the "Human Glitch," this ends his time with the Rockies.

In 2o25, Herget had one of the finest seasons of his career , posting a 2.48 ERA across 83.1 innings. As James Riggenbach wrote earlier this month, Herget gave "the Rockies a dependable multi-inning reliever with a funky delivery and a varied repertoire."

However, it did not carry over into 2026.

Herget finished the season with a 5.70 ERA in 51.0 IP. As James noted, "He pitched well for extended periods, but two particularly difficult stretches did considerable damage to his final numbers." He also became a father, spent time on the Bereavement List, and dealt with a shoulder injury.

With this move, the Rockies maintain a full 40-man roster leading up to the non-tender deadline.

articles.title: 'It's Gonna Hurt Them Again': Celtics Receive Blunt Warning From NBA Legend
articles.summary: The Hall of Fame guard believes Boston's reliance on 3-pointers could come back to haunt it again this season.
articles.body:
Tim Hardaway Sr. isn't a big believer in the Celtics .

On the Nov. 18 episode of the " Crossover Podcast ," the Hall of Fame guard questioned whether Boston's reliance on 3-pointers will allow it to win a championship this season.

"It goes back to saying this: You win by three, you die by the three," Hardaway said.

"I think they so much as that's what they do cuz we saw them last year. They was shooting the hell out the three. They were shooting the hell out the three and then they was winning and then next thing you know they start missing, and it was ugly. It was ugly. So yeah, you live by that three, you die by the three. And I think that's where they are. And I think that's what they — it's gonna hurt them again. It's gonna hurt them again."

The Celtics are averaging 43.9 3-point attempts per game this season, the second-most in the NBA . They've made 37.3 percent of those attempts, the sixth-best percentage in the league .

That high-volume approach has worked for Boston overall, but it can become a problem when the shots stop falling.

The Celtics went 3-for-11 from 3-point range in the fourth quarter of their season-opening loss to the Detroit Pistons, blowing a 22-point lead. They also shot 28.6 percent from deep in their loss to the Houston Rockets and 25.0 percent in their most recent loss to the Denver Nuggets.

Hardaway isn't the only one who has questioned Boston's offensive approach. After the Celtics' first-round loss to the Philadelphia 76ers in the 2026 NBA Playoffs, president of basketball operations Brad Stevens acknowledged that the team needed to find ways to have more of an impact at the rim.

Hardaway isn't convinced the Celtics have done enough to address that issue.

articles.title: Brandon Ingram expected to make season debut for Clippers on Monday vs. Rockets
articles.summary: Ingram has been sidelined since May after undergoing surgery to repair a partially torn Achilles, discovered while getting a bone spur removed from his heel.
articles.body:
Brandon Ingram is expected to make his 2026-27 season debut for the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Before opening training camp, the Clippers announced that Ingram had been diagnosed with a partially torn Achilles tendon in his right leg. The partial tear was discovered while the two-time All-Star underwent surgery to remove a bone spur from his right heel in May.

Ingram was traded by Toronto to the Clippers as part of a package including Gradey Dick, unprotected 2031 and 2033 first-round selections, a 2027 first-round swap and second-round picks in 2030 and 2033 in exchange for Kawhi Leonard.

The deal was originally agreed upon in late June and expected to become official on July 6 when the NBA's moratorium on transactions ended. However, the trade was put on hold amid the NBA's investigation into the Clippers allegedly evading the league's salary cap while signing Leonard to a three-year, $103 million free-agent contract in July 2019.

Both the Clippers and Raptors agreed that the trade wouldn't be completed until the league's probe was completed. The deal finally went through in mid-September, approximately two weeks before NBA teams opened their training camps.

The Clippers knew about Ingram's Achilles tear — repaired in the same procedure that removed his bone spur — before agreeing to the trade, according to interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden. Redden told reporters that Ingram would require about six fewer months of rehab with a partial tear and expected he would play for the Clippers this season.

Ingram averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists for the Raptors last season after being acquired from the New Orleans Pelicans in early 2025. Shortly after joining Toronto, he signed a three-year, $120 million contract extension .

During his 10 NBA seasons, Ingram has averaged 19.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 4.2 assists while shooting 37% on 3-pointers. He was the Los Angeles Lakers' 2016 first-round pick (No. 2 overall) out of Duke. Ingram played three seasons for the Lakers before being traded to New Orleans as part of a three-team deal that sent Anthony Davis to L.A .

Without Ingram, the Clippers are off to a 4-10 start that currently has them as the third-worst team in the Western Conference . The team has also been without Bradley Beal (knee) and Jordan Miller (shoulder) during the opening weeks of the season.

articles.title: El Barça cede en el Palau con polémica al final de la prórroga
articles.standfirst: El Estrella Roja gana en el tiempo extra con Carter liderando (31 puntos) y Parra expulsado en los azulgranas
articles.summary: El Estrella Roja gana en el tiempo extra con Carter liderando (31 puntos) y Parra expulsado en los azulgranas
articles.body: El Barça perdió este viernes contra el Estrella Roja (100-103) en el Palau Blaugrana en un duelo igualado, con múltiples alternancias en el marcador, que se decidió en el último minuto de la prórroga (100-103) y que terminó con protestas en el bando catalán por el criterio de los colegiados. Los azulgranas terminaron molestos con el arbitraje, en especial por los tiros libres concedidos al equipo serbio y por una falta final de Josh Nebo sobre Tyson Carter sancionada como disruptiva, acción que acabó con Joel Parra eliminado por protestar, abandonando la pista enfadado tras mostrarle el escudo a los tres colegiados. El alero catalán, con 20 puntos, destacó junto a Darío Brizuela (22) y Justin Robinson (21) en el conjunto azulgrana, que encadenó la segunda derrota consecutiva en la Euroliga y se alejó a dos triunfos del liderato. Tyson Carter fue el máximo anotador visitante con 31 puntos. Todavía sin el recién fichado Killian Hayes, el Barça tampoco pudo contar con los lesionados Kevin Punter, Umoja Gibson, Tosan Evboumwan y el inédito Yoan Makoundou, mientras que el Estrella Roja también tenía ausencias de calado, como Chima Moneke y Jonathan Motley. Ya fuera por las bajas o por la exigencia del calendario, ambos equipos saltaron a la pista con la mirilla torcida (6-2, min.5), y no se entonaron en ataque hasta la entrada de las segunda unidades. Brizuela revitalizó la ofensiva azulgrana, secundado por Núñez en la dirección y bien conectado en la pintura con Balcerowski (16-4, min.8), pero el cuadro serbio reaccionó gracias a Butler, que enlazó 7 puntos al final del cuarto (23-15). Dos triples de Parra y Minaya situaron la máxima ventaja local al arranque del segundo asalto (29-15, min.11), pero el Estrella Roja replicó con un parcial de 0-9 que forzó el tiempo muerto de Sekulic. El parón no alteró la inercia del duelo, pues al Barça perdonaba lanzamientos liberados y le costaba horrores generar en el ataque estático, más allá de algún chispazo de Brizuela o triple aislado. Y en el Estrella Roja, que imponía su físico en la defensa y el rebote, irrumpieron Carter, con dos triples seguidos, y Ojeleye, con 7 puntos en el cuarto, para voltear el marcador al descanso (40-44). Trató de reaccionar el Barça tras el descanso, impulsado por Parra y Martin, pero el Estrella Roja se mantuvo por delante a base de triples, comandado por Carter, en estado de gracia (49-58, min.24). Lejos de bajar los brazos, los azulgranas endurecieron la defensa, metieron al público en el partido y, liderados en ataque por Brizuela y Robinson, apretaron el marcador al final del tercer cuarto (66-68). El Barça siguió remando hasta situarse por delante en el marcador con dos triples de Robinson y Parra (83-79, min.37), pero cuando lo tenían todo a favor, encadenó un error tras otro -sobre todo Martin, con dos pérdidas y un mal tiro fallado- y el Estrella Roja entró al minuto final en ventaja. Balcerowski, con una canasta y un robo providenciales, empató el partido y Robinson perdonó el triple que habría evitado la prórroga. La igualdad imperó en el tiempo extra, con alternancias constantes hasta el minuto. Dos tiros libres de Butler, un tapón de Koloko a Robinson y una falta disruptiva de Nebo sobre Carter sentenciaron el partido. La acción desembocó en las protestas y la expulsión de Parra, y el Estrella Roja amarró el triunfo desde la línea de personal (100-103). 100. Barça (23+15+26+19+13): Robinson (21), Minaya (6), Parra (20), Martin (4), Nebo (7) -equipo inicial-, Núñez (4), Balcerowski (11), Umude (3), Brizuela (22), Nkamhoua (-), Ubal (2) 103. Estrella Roja (15+29+24+17+18): Jones (-), Weiler-Babb (7), Nwora (13), Ojeleye (9), Koloko (11) -equipo inicial-, Carter (31), Kramer, Izundu (2), Dobric (4), Butler (16), Davidovac (8), Baldwin (2). Árbitros: Emin Mogulkoc (TUR), Ioannis Foufis (GRE) y Christian Theis (ALE). Eliminaron con cinco faltas al local Umude (min.43) y con dos faltas técnicas al local Parra (min.45). Señalaron falta técnica al visitante Kramer (min.31). Incidencias: partido de la jornada 13 de la Euroliga disputado en el Palau Blaugrana de Barcelona ante 4.915 espectadores.

articles.title: Toronto Raptors vs. Detroit Pistons Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors survived a frenetic fourth-quarter battle with the Detroit Pistons to pick up the 105-102 road victory on Friday night. They are now 2-1 in Group Play for the NBA Cup and have a real chance of advancing to the next stage.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors survived a frenetic fourth-quarter battle with the Detroit Pistons to pick up the 105-102 road victory on Friday night. They are now 2-1 in Group Play for the NBA Cup and have a real chance of advancing to the next stage.

Scottie Barnes made his first nine shots and finished with 29 points and five assists on 14-of-21 shooting, including what turned out to be the game-winner—all while spending plenty of time defending Cade Cunningham.

In his first career start, Raptors rookie Allen Graves gap-filled his way to 20 points, 10 rebounds, three steals and one block. Immanuel Quickley had a couple of late-game gaffes but pumped out 18 points and 10 assists.

Cade Cunningham led all scorers with 23 points and also tossed nine dimes. Kevin Huerter came up big with 20 points and three assists. Though Detroit won the three-point, free-throw, offensive rebounding and turnover battles, the margins were so thin that Toronto's first-half shooting and overall plus-10 mark in the paint made all the difference.

Check out all the updates, highlights, analysis, postgame quotes and takeaways you can handle from this one below.

Does "do whatever it takes" include benching Kawhi when he eventually returns to make room for Allen Graves?

THIS GAME WAS ALL SORTS OF HOPPED UP ON CAFFEINE. THAT IS WHY I'M STILL YELLING.

Score: Pistons 102, Raptors 101 | 19.6 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter

I'm not sure if Kevin Huerter called glass, but the angle makes it look like he was certainly trying to hit glass.

Scottie Barnes Continues to Make Tough Shots

This kid has ice and nitrous and the tears of defenders running through his veins.

Score: Pistons 99, Raptors 99 | 1:05 remaining in the fourth quarter

What Do Allen Graves and Scottie Barnes Have in Common?

This stat. And also that they've both been Toronto's two best players this game.

Detroit has nevertheless squeaked ahead. Kevin Huerter made some tough threes before heading to the bench, and the Raptors' offensive process has regressed to mush.

Score: Pistons 99, Raptors 97 | 1:05 remaining in the fourth quarter

This eight-second violation coincided with the official start of crunch time. Raptors head coach Darko Rajaković did not look happy.

In other news, it looks like we're gearing up for one heck of a finish.

Score: Raptors 91, Pistons 88 | 3:58 remaining in the fourth quarter

Not all heroes wear caps. I hear that Jamison Battle sometimes does, but he doesn't have one on right now. He's flying to the rescue for Toronto anyway. His back-to-back corner threes have the Raptors up by seven.

Score: Raptors 87, Pistons 80 | 6:49 remaining in the fourth quarter

The Raptors' Take a 5-Point Lead into the Fourth

Toronto withstood Detroit's late run in the third to bring a five-point lead into the final fame. Scottie Barnes' 21 points and Allen Graves everything are big reasons why they're still ahead, but Immanuel Quickley has quietly racked up nine assists and is a team-best plus-13.

Score: Raptors 77, Pistons 72 | End of the third quarter

Detroit has outscored Toronto by 10 points with Cunningham on the bench in the third quarter. Maybe the Pistons should trade Cade and rebuild around Javonte Green.

Score: Raptors 72, Pistons 70 | 2:01 remaining in the third quarter

Nobody show this to anyone on Cade's family tree.

Toronto has expanded its lead to 10 while keeping Cunningham in check through most of the third quarter.

Score: Raptors 72, Pistons 62 | 3:36 remaining in the third quarter

Scottie Barnes with a MONSTER One-Handed Jam

Even Giannis Antetokounmpo is in awe right now.

In case you're wondering, this dude still hasn't missed. He's 9-of-9 from the floor. His shot chart is greener than Kermit the Frog:

Score: Raptors 67, Pistons 55 | 6:21 remaining in the third quarter

Ausar Thompson looks like he's going to leap straight out of Earth's gravitational field on even the most routine dunks.

We're about ready to fire up the second half. Stay tuned.

Score: Raptors 54, Pistons 48 | Start of the third quarter

The Pistons Have Two Areas to Clean Up in the Second Half

First and foremost, they've given the Raptors a few too many extra possessions. Toronto is rebounding 31.3 percent of its own misses.

The Pistons have also given up too many points in the paint. They are winning the battle overall, 30-28. And to the Raptors' credit, they have hit some ridiculous shots. But Detroit can't hope to win with this differential while trailing in rebounds and (just barely) made threes. The paint needs to be its lifeline, not something it shares with Toronto.

If you think yours truly is pumping up one of his favorite rookies for no reason, then think again. Graves got the walk-off interview with Prime's Cassidy Hubbarth heading into halftime. He deserved it, too.

Scottie Barnes is the only Raptors player to score more points (14 to 10), and nobody on either team has as many rebounds (six). The way Graves is able to box out opponents on both ends of the floor is big-time. Toronto is grabbing 75 percent of Detroit's misses and 33.3 percent of its own misfires during his minutes.

Score: Raptors 54, Pistons 48 | Halftime

Allen Graves has 10 points and a team-leading five boards while playing solid defense in the first half. The Pistons have scored just one point per possessions when he's in the game.

Kawhi might have to back up the rookie when he returns, clearly.

Score: Raptors 49, Pistons 42 | 2:46 remaining in the second quarter

Cade Cunningham Goes Coast-to-Coast(ish)

Cunningham is now up to 11 points on 4-of-5 shooting inside the arc. We'd be talking more about his efficiency if not for Scottie Barnes deciding he's never going to miss a two-point shot ever again.

Score: Raptors 40, Pistons 36 | 6:48 remaining in the second quarter

Scottie Barnes is getting whatever he wants thus far. Thanks in large part to his 7-of-7 clip on twos, the Raptors are shooting 15-17 inside the arc.

That's an 88.2 percent hit rate, for those who care.

Five of these six made field goals from Scottie have come outside the restricted area. He has the mid-range touch tonight and finished the first frame with 12 points to lead all scorers, as well as two assists.

Cade Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins each pumped in six points for Detroit. Neither team is shooting well from three. And both squads already have 16 points in the paint.

The Raptors will enter the second quarter with a three-point lead.

Score: Raptors 26, Pistons 23 | End of the first quarter

Jakob Poeltl has actually been pretty good for the Raptors since returning from his left shoulder injury. Most notably, he no longer moves like he's wearing cinderblocks for shoes.

The proof is in the just-stuffed-Ausar-at-the-rim pudding.

After a slow-ish start, the Pistons are back to doing what they do best: turning stops into offense.

This was a great look from Cade, who has also made his last two shots.

Score: Raptors 16, Pistons 15 | 3:57 remaining in the first quarter

Counterpoint: The NBA Cup courts are loud and great!

The Raptors' Rookie is Already Making an Impact

For those unfamiliar with Allen Graves, he does a little bit of everything. The offensive rebounding and defensive IQ are off the charts, and he's tackled a lot of the toughest covers already this season.

If he can consistently make those corner threes, it'll be hard for the Raptors to keep him off the floor even when they're at full strength.

Scottie is meeting the moment right now. He's got four points and two assists, and he's yet to miss a shot. Cade Cunningham, meanwhile, has started 1-of-3 from the floor.

Score: Raptors 11, Pistons 7 | 7:27 remaining in the first quarter

The Raptors Have Used How Many Starting 5s?!

Taurean Prince never figured to be a huge part of the rotation, but the Pistons traveled modest lengths to land Ebuka Okorie on draft night.

Daniss Jenkins is balling so hard right now this doesn't matter. Still, the Pistons are thin enough when looking at their other injuries. Not having a timeline on Okorie's return to play is less than ideal.

Well, typical during the absences of Jalen Duren and Duncan Robinson anyway.

This will be the fourth game that the group of Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Ausar Thompson and John Collins has started together. The data on the collective isn't great. It has a minus-21.1 net rating, albeit in only 26 minutes of action.

Immanuel Quickley, Ja'Kobe Walter, Scottie Barnes, Allen Graves and Jakob Poeltl have played only eight minutes together , so this should be fun.

Cade Cunningham is Rocking a New Caitlin 1 Colorway

I remain shocked that Caitlin Cooper still allows Cade Cunningham to wear her signature shoe when he's shooting under 32 percent from beyond the arc.

Injury Report for Both the Raptors and Pistons

At least we still get to see Scottie versus Cade, though.

articles.standfirst: Los dos equipos pierden dos partidos esta semana y pierden comba con el líder
articles.summary: Los dos equipos pierden dos partidos esta semana y pierden comba con el líder
articles.body: No es habitual que Real Madrid y Barcelona coincidan con una derrota en la misma jornada de la Euroliga. Mucho menos que haya ocurrido en dos consecutivas. Pero a eso hay que unir que en la jornada 12 y en la 13, sólo el Valencia de los equipos españoles en la máxima competición del baloncesto continental, ha logrado ganar sus dos partidos. Madrid, Barça y Baskonia han vivido una semana 'horribilis', algunos sólo en resultados, otros también en sensaciones y juego. Tal y como fue esta semana de doble jornada, el Valencia y el Olympiacos se han quedado solos al frente de la tabla, con los taronja líderes por el 'average'. Son tres semanas ya con el equipo de Xavi Albert al frente, algo que no había sucedido nunca. Y con su candidatura a todo ganando enteros. El Barça, con su doble derrota en el Palau, ante el Paris Basketball y el Estrella Roja, cede ventaja sobre los dos primeros y baja hasta la séptima posición. También está en zona de Play-In el Madrid, con dos derrotas en Estambul (Besiktas) y Atenas (Olympiacos), más dolorosas por la forma que las del Barcelona. El Madrid se queda noveno a la espera de recibir este miércoles al Zalgiris, que es octavo. El Kosner Baskonia sigue en caída libre: dos derrotas más para sumar ya 12 en 13 partidos y cimentar aún más su condición de colista. A pesar de los refuerzos, los vitorianos siguen cosechando disgustos en Europa donde están muy cerca de decir adiós a cualquier opción de pelear por algo digno.

articles.title: LSU's MiLaysia Fulwiley No Longer Facing Felony Charges for Evading Traffic Stop
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU senior guard MiLaysia Fulwiley will be charged with traffic citations but will not face any felony charges in connection with her arrest Saturday night after she allegedly attempted to evade police officers who tried to pull her over.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU senior guard MiLaysia Fulwiley will be charged with traffic citations but will not face any felony charges in connection with her arrest Saturday night after she allegedly attempted to evade police officers who tried to pull her over.

East Baton Rouge District Attorny Hillar Moore confirmed Friday that he would pursue only misdemeanor charges that include fleeing and resisting an officer, and refer Fulwiley to a diversion program to resolve those.

Initially, Fulwiley also was booked with aggravated battery and assault for allegedly driving her vehicle into that of an officer.

State police captain Russell Graham said Friday that his agency reviewed evidence with Moore and agreed with his decision.

"After a thorough review with all involved parties, the charges were amended based on the circumstances and evidence presented," State Police said in a written statement provided by Graham.

Fulwiley has not played since her arrest and it is not clear when she will return to the team.

"Saturday night ended in a situation that never should have happened," Fulwiley said in a statement released by LSU. "I owe an apology to the officers involved and everyone who calls themselves a Tiger. I also want to apologize to my family and all those who love and support me."

The traffic stop occurred near 102,000-seat Tiger Stadium as the a football game between LSU and Texas was ending.

"Rules and laws apply to everyone, including the instructions of officers working a game night in Baton Rouge," Fulwiley said. "I respect the job those officers do, and I'll let the legal process run its course. My focus is doing what this program asks of me and earning back the trust of the people who count on me."

Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points per game this season and scored a season-high 23 points during No. 9 LSU's 101-37 victory over Denver on Nov. 13.

articles.title: James Harden Scores 51 Points, Passes Kobe Bryant on Historic NBA List in Cavs vs. Pacers
articles.summary: Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden has now broken a third-place tie with Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant for the most 50-plus point games in NBA history after dropping 51 in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday evening.
articles.body:
Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden has now broken a third-place tie with Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant for the most 50-plus point games in NBA history after dropping 51 in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday evening.

Harden has now accomplished the feat 26 times. Wilt Chamberlain is first on the list (118), and Michael Jordan is second (31). Elgin Baylor rounds out the top five (17).

On Friday, Harden shot 15-of-26 (7-of-11 from three-point range) and made all 14 of his free throws. He added six rebounds and assists apiece, and the Cavs outscored the Pacers by 22 points with him on the floor.
